portName: Cherbourg cruise terminal (Quai de France, Gare Maritime Transatlantique)
seoTitle: Cherbourg cruise port guide: Cité de la Mer, D-Day, Bayeux
seoDescription: Cherbourg cruise port is 1.2 km from the centre, 10–15 min on foot. Cité de la Mer €21 (2026) next to the ship. Bayeux 53–55 min by train; Utah Beach €10.
quickAnswer: Ships berth at the Quai de France and passengers come ashore through the Art Deco Gare Maritime Transatlantique, which also houses the Cité de la Mer. The town centre is about 1.2 km away, a flat 10–15 minute walk, and on many calls a shuttle runs as well. For a train or bus trip, be back at Cherbourg station at least two hours before all-aboard; for the town, be back on board an hour before.
intro: Cherbourg's cruise berth has the most striking arrival hall in northern France: you walk ashore through the former transatlantic liner terminal, now the Cité de la Mer, where the submarine Le Redoutable and a Titanic exhibition sit metres from the gangway. The port takes one cruise ship a day. The town itself is small and walkable. Most passengers come for the D-Day sites of the Cotentin peninsula, with Utah Beach the closest landing beach; Omaha Beach and Mont-Saint-Michel are much further and only make sense on an organised tour. Bayeux is an easy train trip, and Barfleur is reachable by local bus on a long call.

terminals.name: Cruise terminal, Quai de France (Gare Maritime Transatlantique)
terminals.notes: 600 m berth with covered electric gangways into the renovated terminal in the Cité de la Mer's former baggage hall, reopened in September 2024. A tourist office desk is inside. Taxis and excursion coaches wait outside. Some ships use the neighbouring Quai de Normandie.

walkability.detail: A flat 10–15 minute walk along the waterfront past the Bassin du Commerce to the centre. The train station is about 2 km, 20–25 minutes on foot.

transportSections.detail: Follow the waterfront from the terminal along the Bassin du Commerce. The Cité de la Mer is in the terminal building itself.

transportSections.mode: Cruise shuttle (tourist office and Cap Cotentin)
transportSections.cost: Check at the terminal tourist office
transportSections.detail: On many calls the Cotentin tourist office runs a shuttle with the Cap Cotentin network between the terminal and the centre, with stops at the tourist information office and the bus station. It does not run on every call; ask at the terminal desk.

transportSections.cost: €1 for one hour, €1.50 bought on board, €4 for 24 hours (2025 fares)
transportSections.detail: The local network for Cherbourg and the Cotentin. Line 12 runs from Cherbourg station to Barfleur. Check timetables on capcotentin.fr.

transportSections.cost: Check SNCF Connect for the fare
transportSections.detail: About 9 direct TER trains a day from Cherbourg station, first at 06:52, calling at Valognes, Carentan and Lison on the way. Gaps between trains can be long, so plan the return first.

transportSections.cost: Agree or check the fare before setting off
transportSections.time: Short ride to the station or centre
transportSections.detail: Taxis wait outside the terminal, but there may not be enough for everyone on a big-ship day. Book a driver in advance for a D-Day day.

returnTiming.rule: If you leave Cherbourg by train or bus, be back at Cherbourg station at least 2 hours before all-aboard. From the town centre, be back on board 60 minutes before all-aboard.
returnTiming.detail: Trains to Bayeux and buses to Barfleur run only a handful of times a day, so missing one can mean a gap of an hour or more. The station is a 20–25 minute walk from the ship, or a short taxi ride.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: If your train or bus is late, call the port agent number on your daily programme at once and take a taxi from the station straight to the Quai de France.

excursionAdvice: Take the ship's tour, or a pre-booked private guide, for the D-Day beaches. Public transport to Utah and Omaha beaches is not practical on a cruise day, the sites are spread out, and Omaha and the American Cemetery are a long way east. Mont-Saint-Michel is 2.5–3 hours by road each way, so only go with the ship, which will wait for its coaches. The Cité de la Mer, the town, Fort du Roule and Bayeux are easy on your own.

dayPlan.intro: Assumes the ship docks at 08:00 and all-aboard is 17:30, on a day between Tuesday and Friday in summer, spent in Cherbourg.

steps.what: Cité de la Mer opens: go aboard the submarine Le Redoutable first, before the queues, then the Titanic exhibition and aquariums.
Walk 10–15 minutes into the centre along the Bassin du Commerce; lunch in the old streets near Place du Général de Gaulle.
Taxi or a steep walk up the Montagne du Roule to the Liberation Museum in Fort du Roule (reopens at 14:00 on weekdays) for the view over the harbour.
Back down into town for a last walk around the centre and the marina.

sights.name: La Cité de la Mer
sights.why: Ocean and seafaring museum in the 1930s transatlantic terminal, with Le Redoutable, a decommissioned nuclear submarine you can walk through, a Titanic exhibition and large aquariums.
sights.cost: €21 adult, €15 child 5–17; €30 with the VR experience (2026)
sights.tip: The ticket is valid all day with re-entry. Arrive at opening; last entry is 90 minutes before closing. Children under 5 cannot board the submarine.

sights.name: Musée de la Libération (Fort du Roule)
sights.why: Museum of the 1944 liberation of Cherbourg in a fort on the hill above the town, with a view over the harbour.
sights.cost: €5 adult, free on Wednesdays and for under-26s (2025)
sights.tip: Closed on Mondays; on weekdays it closes 12:30–14:00. About 25 minutes on foot from the station, uphill.

sights.name: Utah Beach Museum
sights.why: The D-Day landing museum on the beach at Sainte-Marie-du-Mont, the closest landing beach to Cherbourg.
sights.tip: Open daily 09:30–19:00 from May to September and 10:00–18:00 from October to April; closed 16 November to 14 December. Go with a tour or a booked driver.

sights.name: Bayeux
sights.why: Medieval town with its cathedral and the Bayeux Tapestry museum, under an hour by train.
sights.tip: Pick your return train before you set out; there are only about 9 a day.

sights.name: Barfleur and Gatteville lighthouse
sights.why: Fishing harbour where William the Conqueror gathered his fleet in 1066, and a 75 m lighthouse 2 km away.
sights.cost: Lighthouse €3.50 (2026); check the bus fare on capcotentin.fr
sights.tip: Cap Cotentin line 12 takes about 45 minutes from Cherbourg station and runs only a few times a day. The lighthouse gallery closes in winds above 50 km/h.

sights.name: Cherbourg town centre and marina
sights.why: Compact centre of shopping streets and squares beside the harbour and marina.
sights.tip: Start at the tourist information office, a stop on the cruise shuttle.

sights.name: Mont-Saint-Michel
sights.why: The abbey island on the border of Normandy and Brittany.
sights.cost: Ship excursion price; check your cruise planner
sights.tip: 2.5–3 hours by road each way. Only attempt it on the ship's own tour.

beaches.name: Utah Beach
beaches.howToGetThere: Ship tour, private driver or hire car
beaches.time: Check the drive time with your driver
beaches.note: A wide sandy D-Day beach; most visitors come for the museum and memorials.

beaches.name: Barfleur cove
beaches.howToGetThere: Cap Cotentin bus 12, then walk north of the marine cemetery
beaches.cost: Free beach; check the bus fare on capcotentin.fr
beaches.note: Small sandy cove with a view of the Gatteville lighthouse.

commonMistakes.mistake: Trying to reach Omaha Beach or Mont-Saint-Michel independently.
commonMistakes.fix: Both are too far for public transport on a cruise day. Book the ship's tour or a reputable private guide.
It runs on many calls but not all. The walk is only 10–15 minutes anyway.

commonMistakes.mistake: Missing the last useful train or bus.
commonMistakes.fix: Bayeux trains and Barfleur buses are infrequent. Plan to be back at Cherbourg station two hours before all-aboard.

commonMistakes.mistake: Visiting the Liberation Museum on a Monday or at lunchtime.
commonMistakes.fix: It is closed on Mondays and from 12:30 to 14:00 on weekdays; weekends it opens at 13:00.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the Cité de la Mer until the end of the day.
commonMistakes.fix: It needs about four hours and last entry is 90 minutes before closing. Go first thing, since it is next to the ship.

safety: Cherbourg is a small, quiet French port town and safe for visitors. Take normal care with bags in busy places. At the D-Day sites, stay on marked paths; dunes and old fortifications can be uneven. The walk up to Fort du Roule is steep.
accessibility: The terminal has covered electric gangways, and the walk to the centre is flat. The Cité de la Mer main halls are on level floors; the submarine has narrow passages and is not suitable for everyone. Reduced prices apply with proof of disability at the Cité de la Mer, and the Liberation Museum is free for visitors with disabilities and a companion. The Fort du Roule hill and the 365 steps of Gatteville lighthouse are not accessible.
rainyDay: Cherbourg is a good rainy-day port: the Cité de la Mer is indoors, next to the ship, and fills most of a day. Add the Liberation Museum, or take the train to Bayeux for the tapestry and cathedral.
crowdTips: Cherbourg takes one cruise ship a day, with about 75 calls expected in 2026, so the town rarely feels crowded. The Cité de la Mer is busiest once ship tours return; go at opening. Taxis can run short when a large ship is in, so pre-book a driver for D-Day sites.

faqs.q: Is Cherbourg walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. The centre is about 1.2 km away, a flat 10–15 minute walk.
No. Ships berth at the Quai de France beside the Cité de la Mer.

faqs.q: Can I visit the D-Day beaches from Cherbourg cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes, by ship tour, private guide or hire car. Utah Beach is the closest landing beach; Omaha is much further east. Public transport is not practical.

faqs.q: Can I get to Mont-Saint-Michel from Cherbourg on a cruise?
faqs.a: Only on an organised tour. It is 2.5–3 hours by road each way.

faqs.q: How do I get from Cherbourg to Bayeux?
faqs.a: Direct TER train from Cherbourg station, 53–55 minutes, about 9 a day.

faqs.q: What can I do in Cherbourg in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Cité de la Mer next to the ship, the town centre, and the Liberation Museum at Fort du Roule.

faqs.q: How much is the Cité de la Mer?
faqs.a: €21 for adults and €15 for children aged 5–17 in 2026.
Yes. It is a small, quiet port town.
